scan_metadata.paper: Adaptive Linear Path Model-Based Diffusion (Shimizu & Tomizuka), arXiv 2602.02831
scan_metadata.explanation: All 61 tracked files were listed. The READMEs, all 8 entry scripts, the YAML configs and the implementation paths behind the selected commands were read; some controller internals (MPPI, Brax VP/MPPI/CEM/CMA-ES, ActorCritic.evaluate) were read only in outline. Seven documented commands are selected as execution sources and proposed as seven cli_wrapper tools (Figs. 3-6 and Tables I-II of the paper). RL fine-tuning (run_rl_fine_tuning.py) is deferred because of its training cost and because it overwrites the shipped checkpoint. Path generators and module __main__ self-tests are omitted as setup or internal code. No repository code was executed during the scan; all feasibility numbers are estimates unless they quote a workspace measurement.
scan_metadata.provenance_note: The paper's anonymous repository (anonymous.4open.science/r/adaptive_linear_path_model_based_diffusion-C58C) has expired (HTTP 410). This public repository by the first author has the same name and is used instead. It is not established that it is byte-identical to the paper's artifact.
scan_metadata.licence_note: The repository has NO licence file (no LICENSE/COPYING among the 61 tracked files at the pinned commit). Redistribution of its code, checkpoint and figures inside a delivered package is not covered by any licence. The coordinator should record this in USAGE.md and decide whether the ZIP references the checkout instead of bundling it.
scan_metadata.heavy_job_gate_note: mcp-build/HEAVY_JOBS_DISABLED exists (coordinator, 2026-10-02T15:10Z). heavy.sh refuses every command while it exists (exit 75). This blocks the Brax/JAX command now. The PyTorch commands are not JAX jobs, but the machine had about 2.6 GB available at scan time (free -m), so run them one at a time.

tutorials.title: 1D examples: VP-MBD vs LP-MBD (paper Fig. 3)
tutorials.description: python run_1d_example.py --name {gaussian,gaussian_mixture,sin_mixture}. Runs VP-MBD and LP-MBD on a fixed 1D objective and saves a 3-panel figure (objective, VP trajectories, LP trajectories) to images/1d/<name>_results_1d.png next to the script.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Documented command. It reproduces the paper's Fig. 3 (one row per --name). The figure is the only output, and the shipped reference images make it verifiable.

suggested_tools.description: Run VP-MBD and LP-MBD on a fixed 1D objective (gaussian, gaussian_mixture or sin_mixture) and return the 3-panel comparison figure (paper Fig. 3).
suggested_tools.primary_input: name: one of gaussian | gaussian_mixture | sin_mixture
outputs: images/1d/<name>_results_1d.png (inside the per-call copy of tutorial/)

tutorials.title: 2D examples: VP-MBD vs LP-MBD (paper Fig. 4 for constrained_gaussian_mixture_2d)
tutorials.description: python run_2d_example.py --name {gaussian_2d,constrained_gaussian_2d,gaussian_mixture_2d,constrained_gaussian_mixture_2d}. Saves a 2x3 panel figure (VP top row, LP bottom row) to images/2d/<name>_result.png next to the script.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Documented command. For --name constrained_gaussian_mixture_2d it reproduces Fig. 4: it uses the learned parameters from the Fig. 4 caption (sigma_max=2.1113, beta0=2.8e-5, beta1=0.3609, T=3), and the shipped PNG visually matches Fig. 4. The other three names are additional examples.

suggested_tools.description: Run VP-MBD and LP-MBD on a fixed 2D objective and return the 2x3 panel figure. constrained_gaussian_mixture_2d reproduces paper Fig. 4 with the learned schedule parameters.
suggested_tools.primary_input: name: one of gaussian_2d | constrained_gaussian_2d | gaussian_mixture_2d | constrained_gaussian_mixture_2d
outputs: images/2d/<name>_result.png (inside the per-call copy of tutorial/)

tutorials.title: ALP-MBD: learn (sigma_max, T) with REINFORCE on the constrained 2D Gaussian mixture
tutorials.description: python run_alp_mbd.py (no arguments). Runs 30 REINFORCE updates of the ALPMBD tuner around LP-MBD, prints 'sigma_max_opt: <float>, T_opt: <tensor>' and saves images/2d/ALP_MBD_results_2d.png next to the script.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Documented command. It implements the Sec. V-A adaptive experiment (the Fig. 4 caption reports sigma_max=2.11, T=3 for ALP-MBD after 30 training steps) and is the paper's own method on the toy problem.

suggested_tools.description: Learn ALP-MBD schedule parameters (sigma_max, T) with 30 REINFORCE updates on the constrained 2D Gaussian mixture. Returns the learned values and a 4-panel sampling figure.

tutorials.title: AVP-MBD baseline: learn (beta0, beta1, T) with REINFORCE on the constrained 2D Gaussian mixture
tutorials.description: python run_avp_mbd.py (no arguments). Runs 30 REINFORCE updates of the AVPMBD tuner around VP-MBD, prints 'beta0_opt: .., beta1_opt: .., T_opt: ..' and saves images/2d/AVP_MBD_results_2d.png next to the script.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Documented command. It is the Sec. V-A baseline: the Fig. 4 caption reports beta0=0.000028, beta1=0.361, T=3 for AVP-MBD.

suggested_tools.description: Baseline: learn AVP-MBD schedule parameters (beta0, beta1, T) with the same REINFORCE budget. Returns the learned values and a 4-panel sampling figure.

tutorials.title: Path tracking with MPPI / VP-MBD / LP-MBD (paper Table II, VP-MBD and LP-MBD rows)
tutorials.description: From the vehicle_control directory: python run_experiment.py --config config/{mppi,vp_mbd,lp_mbd}_controller.yaml [--seed N] [--device cuda|cpu] [--save_mode True]. Runs one episode of the kinematic-vehicle path-tracking environment and prints the episode reward, the episode length and the average solve time per control step [ms]. It can also write a GIF to ./video/seed_<seed>_<filename>.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Documented command. The shipped vp_mbd/lp_mbd configs carry the Table II settings (T=17, horizon 50, 100 samples, beta 1e-4/1e-2, sigma_max 1.8). Table II averages over 5 seeds via --seed. It accepts a different reference path through the documented ref_path key.

suggested_tools.description: Run one closed-loop path-tracking episode with MPPI, VP-MBD or LP-MBD and report episode reward, episode length and average solve time per step. Optionally writes a GIF. Paper Table II VP/LP rows over seeds.
suggested_tools.primary_input: controller (mppi|vp_mbd|lp_mbd); reference_path (s_bend|oval|straight or a user CSV x,y,yaw,v with >=302 rows); seed; device (cuda|cpu); save_gif; optional documented YAML keys (diffusion_steps, sigma_max, beta0, beta1, temperature, num_samples, horizon, max_episode_length) via a config copy
outputs: parsed stdout: episode reward, episode length, average solve time [ms], average episode reward/length, goal/collision events
optional video/seed_<seed>_<filename>.gif in the per-call cwd

tutorials.title: ALP-MBD with the shipped PPO tuner: per-step (T, sigma_max) along the path (paper Figs. 5 and 6)
tutorials.description: python run_rl_evaluation.py --config config/lp_mbd_fine_tuning_evaluation.yaml [--seed N] [--device cuda|cpu]. Loads data/fine_tuner_checkpoints/lp_mbd_fine_tuner.pth, runs one LP-MBD episode with per-step parameters from the tuner, prints average sigma_max, diffusion step and calculation time, and saves video/<ref basename>_rl_evaluation.png next to the script.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Documented command, and the trained tuner ships with the repository. With ref_path=data/path/oval_path.csv (default) it reproduces Fig. 6. With ref_path=data/path/s_bend_path.csv it reproduces Fig. 5. Both reference PNGs ship in vehicle_control/video/.

suggested_tools.description: Run ALP-MBD with the shipped PPO noise-schedule tuner for one episode. Returns the trajectory figure coloured by diffusion step and sigma_max (paper Fig. 5 on s_bend, Fig. 6 on oval) and the per-step averages.
suggested_tools.primary_input: reference_path (oval = default config | s_bend); seed; device. The checkpoint is fixed at data/fine_tuner_checkpoints/lp_mbd_fine_tuner.pth
outputs: video/<ref basename>_rl_evaluation.png (inside the per-call copy of vehicle_control/)
parsed stdout: average calculation time [ms], Average sigma_max, Average diffusion step (the printed 'average episode reward' is a partial-sum mean, not an episode reward)

tutorials.title: Brax comparison of LP-MBD, VP-MBD, MPPI, CEM, CMA-ES (paper Table I)
tutorials.description: python main.py --env_name <env> --controller {lp_mbd,vp_mbd,mppi,cem,cma_es} [--horizon 50] [--sample_size 2000] [--total_diffusion_steps 50] --disable_wandb. Runs seeds 0-4, 50 receding-horizon control steps each, and prints the per-seed average reward plus the final mean and std (Table I format). Writes no files.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Documented command, and the only implementation of Table I. Selected but EXECUTION BLOCKED for now: it is a JAX/Brax heavy job and HEAVY_JOBS_DISABLED is set. The default problem size (about 1.2e9 simulated env steps per call) is infeasible here, so a reference run needs the reduced --sample_size/--horizon/--total_diffusion_steps values given in tool_review. The coordinator should record an exclusion if the gate stays closed.

suggested_tools.description: Receding-horizon control of a Brax task with lp_mbd, vp_mbd, mppi, cem or cma_es over seeds 0-4. Returns per-seed and final mean/std per-step reward (paper Table I). Heavy JAX job: currently blocked by HEAVY_JOBS_DISABLED and only feasible with reduced sample_size/horizon/total_diffusion_steps.
suggested_tools.primary_input: env_name (ant|hopper|halfcheetah|walker2d|reacher|pusher|inverted_double_pendulum|inverted_pendulum); controller (lp_mbd|vp_mbd|mppi|cem|cma_es); horizon; sample_size; total_diffusion_steps (wrapper always adds --disable_wandb)
outputs: parsed stdout: Seed k Average reward (x5), Final Average reward, Final Reward std
